https://atomicdata.dev/integrations/prop: Reads your own time entries in one workspace over a rolling 7- or 30-day look-back, keeps what each read saw in an observation log in the drive, and shows a week grid, the entries by day and hours per project. Completed entries become rows in the app's table (start, end, project, billable). A timeline shows overlapping entries and work over a break as conflicts, and time no read has covered as not loaded, never as not worked. An entry's description, project, billable flag, start and end can be edited in the app or in the table, or the entry deleted; a time range can be marked as worked on a project or as not worked, which trims, splits, extends or creates entries over exactly that range; and a conflict can be resolved by keeping one project, marking it not worked, or removing a duplicate. Each change is listed under Changes to send and written to Clockify only when sent, after a fresh read, and confirmed by a read afterwards. If Clockify changed the same field, Clockify's value is kept; a new entry is not created where Clockify has time by then. With the app open on two devices or in two tabs, one sends at a time, and range edits made on each without seeing the other's are shown as a conflict between your edits and held until one is chosen.

Running timers, locked entries, breaks and entries with custom field values cannot be edited. Coordination between two open copies is advisory (the drive has no compare-and-swap), so two copies starting to send in the same moment can still both send, at worst creating a duplicate that the app then offers to remove; it has been tested with simulated devices only, not with two real browsers. The same field edited directly on two devices keeps the later edit. No tags, tasks, rates or custom fields. Tested against a mock proxy modelled on Clockify behaviour checked against a live account (2026-09-24); the app itself has not run against a live account or the real integration proxy.

Notion has no conditional page updates, so an edit made in Notion in the moment between the check and the send is overwritten. All shared databases go into one table.
